title: Israeli man shot dead near West Bank settlement, Netanyahu orders demolition of âterroristâ home
text: Israeli police officer and a soldier stand guard near the site of a shooting attack that killed one Israeli. (AP Photo) An Israeli man in his 30s was shot dead near the West Bank settlement of Neve Tzuf, also known as Halamish, on Sunday, hours before the start of the Yom Kippur holiday. The suspected attacker, who was injured while fleeing the scene, was later arrested at a hospital, according to the Israeli military. The victim was identified as Netanel Shukrun, a father of six who lived in the West Bank settlement of Alei Zahav, The Times of Israel reported. Shukrun had gone to a natural spring near Neve Tzuf with his eldest son to immerse in the water ahead of Yom Kippur, when the shooting took place. How the attack unfolded According to the Israel Defense Forces, the suspected attacker opened fire toward the spring from a vehicle before getting out and fleeing on foot while still armed. Shukrun was seriously wounded and taken to Beilinson Hospital in Petah Tikva, where he later died. Footage shared on social media showed people at the spring ducking for cover as gunshots were heard in the area. The military said a combat tracker from the Binyamin Regional Brigade opened fire at the attacker as he fled, injuring him. The suspect then returned to his vehicle and drove to a hospital near Ramallah, where Israeli commandos from the Duvdevan Unit later arrested him based on information from the Shin Bet. The suspect's vehicle parked outside the hospital was also seized, the IDF said. Separately, the military said soldiers shot dead a Palestinian man who allegedly attempted to ram troops with his vehicle near the site of the former settlement of Ganim in the northern West Bank. Another Palestinian who was in the vehicle was detained, while no Israeli soldiers were injured, according to the IDF. What Netanyahu said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the attacks and said that "no terrorist is immune, nor are those who assisted them." Netanyahu said he had instructed Israeli security forces to send reinforcements to the West Bank, impose closures and carry out arrests. âWe will hold them all accountable â in Gaza, in Lebanon, and in Judea and Samaria,â he said in a statement. He also ordered the immediate demolition of the home of "the terrorist", though it was unclear which of the two attackers he was referring to. "On behalf of all the citizens of Israel, my wife and I send our deepest condolences to the family of the victim of the attack and share in their profound grief," Netanyahu said. Shukrun worked as a systems information analyst, while his wife Meirav is a lecturer at Ariel University, according to The Times of Israel. title: Operation Sheruwali: How security forces tracked LeT commander Musa in months-long hunt since May
text: Hashim Moosa (Left) killed in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmirâs Budgam district, Indian Army (File photo) NEW DELHI: The killing of senior Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Musa in Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district on Wednesday was the culmination of a months-long intelligence-led operation, named âOperation Sheruwaliâ, launched in May 2026. Security forces had been tracking Musa for a prolonged period before a coordinated plan involving multiple agencies was drawn up to neutralise him, following the receipt of technical and human intelligence about his movements and presence in the area. The operation culminated in an encounter in the Yousmarg area of Budgam, where Musa was killed. His body was later recovered along with war-like stores, according to the Army. Also read| Ex-Pakistan SSG commando, highly trained LeT terrorist, Pahalgam mastermind: Who was Hashim Moosa; killed in J&K encounter The ministry of information and broadcasting said the operation dealt a blow to the LeT network in Jammu and Kashmir, with Musa's killing bringing an end to a group of four senior commanders who had been operating in the union territory since 2022 and were linked to several attacks. Watch Operation Sheruwali Intensifies In Rajouri As Army Tightens Cordon Around Suspected Militants How Operation Sheruwali unfolded According to a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), security forces had been pursuing Musa for a long time. A specific plan involving all stakeholders was recently put in place after intelligence inputs indicated his movement and presence. The government said the operation to neutralise Musa was part of the ongoing âOperation Sheruwaliâ, which began in May 2026. The Army's Chinar Corps, meanwhile, said the encounter took place during Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam district. Troops launched a search operation based on specific intelligence inputs and challenged suspicious movement, following which terrorists opened fire. The operation involved the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). The search continued after the encounter, with security personnel checking the surrounding areas for any additional terrorist presence. Musa's body was recovered from the general area of Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Chinar Corps. Is Hashim Moosa an ex-Pakistan SSG commando? One of the key aspects of Musa's background is his alleged association with Pakistan's military. ANI, quoting security agency sources, reported that Musa had served as a para-commando in Pakistan's Special Service Group (SSG), where he held the rank of Havildar. According to the sources, he retired from the SSG in 2023, subsequently joined the LeT and infiltrated into India. Former Jammu and Kashmir DGP S P Vaid described Musa as a highly trained commando specialising in ambushes and guerrilla-style attacks. Vaid alleged that Musa's footprints had been seen in several attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, including those in Poonch, DKG, Bhimber Gali, Gulmarg and the attack on pilgrims in Reasi. However, his alleged military background has been reported by security agency sources and has not been independently established. Four-member LeT group neutralised With Musa's killing, all four senior LeT commanders belonging to the group that had been active in Jammu and Kashmir since 2022 have been neutralised, according to the government. The three other commanders were killed in separate encounters: Junaid Bhat: Neutralised on December 3, 2024, in Dachigam. Suleman: Killed on July 28, 2025, during Operation Mahadev. Yasir: Neutralised on September 4, 2026, during Operation Asdhar. The government linked the group to several attacks across Jammu and Kashmir, including the Halan attack in August 2023, DKG attack in December 2023, Kandi attack in May 2023, Shahsitar attack in May 2024, Shiv Khori attack in June 2024, Gagangir and Bootapathri attacks in October 2024, and the Baisaran attack in April 2025. Musa's alleged role in Pahalgam attack Musa was among the key suspects in the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack , in which terrorists targeted tourists at Baisaran Valley, killing 26 people. The Jammu and Kashmir Police had announced a reward of Rs 20 lakh for information leading to the arrest of Pakistan nationals and LeT terrorists Adil Hussain Thoker, Ali Bhai and Hashim Musa. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) subsequently chargesheeted seven accused in the case, including Pakistan-based LeT and The Resistance Front (TRF), which it accused of planning, facilitating and executing the attack. title: âThey are all chasing the CMâs chairâ: Punjab BJP chief Kewal Dhillon accuses Congress of infighting after Warringâs resignation
text: Punjab BJP chief targets Congress over Warring resignation, alleges infighting over CM post NEW DELHI: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Friday alleged infighting within the Congress following Amarinder Singh Raja Warring's resignation as Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president, accusing leaders in the opposition party of being focused on the chief minister's post. "I have always said regarding the Congress that once they secure one person's resignation, they will go after another. There is infighting over the chair within their ranks. They are all merely chasing the Chief Minister's chair; they have no concern for Punjab," Dhillon said. Warring resigned as Punjab Congress president on Friday after heading the state unit for more than four years. He later met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and formally handed in his resignation. Dhillon questioned whether Warring's resignation would bring an end to the developments within the Congress. "Do you think this will end with just one resignation? It is only going to escalate further," he said. BJP raises law and order issue Dhillon also alleged that the law and order situation in Punjab was "dire" and raised the issue of crimes against Dalits. "The situation in Punjab is dire. In the Chief Minister's own district, crimes against Dalits are occurring daily. Today, there is virtually no law and order left in the entire state of Punjab," he said. His remarks came as the Congress prepares to reorganise its Punjab unit ahead of the assembly polls due early next year. Warring's resignation followed longstanding differences within the state Congress. Warring says he conveyed his views to Rahul Gandhi Earlier on Friday, Warring claimed that AICC Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may have decided that it was time for him to be removed as state Congress chief. Speaking to ANI, Warring said he had already conveyed his views to Rahul Gandhi and acknowledged that he did not have concrete proof that Pilot had taken the decision. "When he was appointed in charge, I went to formally congratulate him. I spoke with him for about 15 minutes that day. But I haven't met him since. Given my long journey in politics, I feel that Sachin Pilot must have decided it was time to remove 'Raja' from the post. I don't have concrete proof of this, but perhaps the General Secretary felt that Raja should be removed. Otherwise, there is no specific issue. I have conveyed what I had to say to Rahul Gandhi. There is no one left after Rahul Gandhi to whom I could explain what should or shouldn't happen," Warring said. Warring also said Gandhi showed him âa lot of loveâ during their meeting. According to PTI, he told Gandhi about the challenges facing the Congress in Punjab, its strengths and the political situation in the state. "I met Rahul Gandhi and formally gave him my resignation," Warring told reporters after the meeting, according to PTI. He said Gandhi sought information about the political situation in Punjab, including what was happening with the government and what the Congress should be doing. title: Land victory is the only tangible factor in war: Army chief; says no substitute for self-reliance in weapon development
text: Army chief General Dhiraj Seth NEW DELHI: Amid the continuing Ukraine-Russia war over land boundaries and Iran-US conflict over the control of the Strait of Hormuz, Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Seth said on Sunday that despite modern technological disruptions, physical territorial control remains the ultimate measure of military triumph and âland victory is the only tangible factorâ in war. In his address at NDTV Defence Summit, General Seth said: âWe see salvo after salvo in todayâs social media covering warfare across the globe, where information narratives and warfare are being fired to fog the real battle picture, creating uncertainty and confusion...However, I strongly feel, through all this clutter, one reality that does not change: land will always be the one and only tangible and useful factor of success. Victory was, is, and will always be measured in territorial terms and that territory will be occupied, secured, and defended only by the force.â Gen Seth said technology is certainly shortening battles but it is not necessarily shortening wars, and that âland victory is the only indisputable marker of war victoryâ. âThese millennium wars can best be described as wars with pause. Pause, in fact, is becoming a part of military strategy, with the pause representing not the domination of conflict but merely a change in its intensity and manifestation,â he said. Underlining that there is no substitute for self-reliance, the Army chief said, âAtmanirbharta must be about ensuring that we have the capability to endure without being constrained by what others can or cannot provide. That gives us a good reason to take a hard look at the very pathways of our indigenous capability. Aatmanirbharta must mean design in India, develop in India, manufacture in India, sustain in India, upgrade in India, and also make for the world. â However, Gen Seth advised caution regarding âindigenous obsolescenceâ. âThe challenge is not just to reduce dependencies on others but also to ensure that what we develop indigenously does not become outdated by the time it is dumped. I would like to term it as indigenous obsolescence or that kind of a trap that can get created,â he said. Talking about a photo taken on Dec 16, 1971, that depicted Pakistan surrendering during the Bangladesh war, Gen Seth said: âThe reason I allude to this today is that that photo gave us a very defining moment, because that was the precise moment when the war came to an end. But there is no demarcating moment; there is no termination point which indicates an end to the hostilities.â

title: Oil prices ease slightly as G7 and Middle East crude supplies set to hit market
text: Crude prices ease marginally on Monday Oil prices found marginal relief on Monday as concerns over global energy supplies eased with more crude entering the market. Additional shipments from the Middle East, along with the Group of Sevenâs decision to release oil from emergency reserves, helped offset concerns over possible further damage to energy infrastructure in the Gulf amid the Iran war. As of 7:15 am IST, Brent Crude was down 0.54% at $101.70 while WTI Crude fell 0.92% to $90.27. The G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency stocks came last week, following pressure from US President Donald Trump. The countries also pledged not to impose energy export restrictions. The G7 move comes as Middle Eastern crude exports have already picked up. Shipping data showed that exports were above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the final week of September, despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz. The market remains exposed to developments around the Gulf. The Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia, saying the attacks were in response to 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen over the previous 12 hours. Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday that it was beginning a major military campaign to retake all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis. Aramco has also unexpectedly reduced its November crude oil prices for Asia to six-year lows, Reuters reported. Meanwhile, OPEC+ has postponed a review that was expected to determine oil output quotas for its members in 2027. Two sources close to the matter said the US-Israeli war on Iran had disrupted projects intended to expand production capacity across the Middle East, making estimates of future production potential uncertain. Developments in Europe are also shaping oil markets. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Reuters that Ukraine would step up attacks on Russian oil refineries. Brent had surrendered most of its gains from the previous week, while WTI was 1.6% lower after the G7 decision. As the Middle East conflict stretches beyond the seven-month mark, the oil market has remained volatile. title: Vizag coast retreated 64m in 35 years, faces high vulnerability: Study
text: Vizag coast retreated 64m in 35 years, faces high vulnerability: Study Visakhapatnam: The coastline of Vizag retreated by an average of 64 metres between 1990 and 2024, with some stretches eroding at rates of up to 13.1 metres a year, according to a 35-year coastal vulnerability assessment. The study identified Rushikonda, RK Beach, Yarada and Bheemilipatnam among the stretches facing high coastal vulnerability. Researchers assessed the Visakhapatnam and Uppada coasts using satellite imagery, GIS-based shoreline analysis and field validation. Landsat images from 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2024 were analysed using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System to track shoreline changes. The assessment considered shoreline change, coastal slope, land use and land cover, relative sea level and tidal range. The study found significant variations along the Vizag coast. Zone II, covering the Gangavaram port area, recorded both the highest erosion rate of 13.1 metres a year and the highest accretion rate of 21.1 metres a year. During the study period, the zone witnessed shoreline displacement of up to 383.2 metres towards erosion and 604.7 metres towards accretion, indicating complex sediment movement. Researchers said human interventions have played a key role in reshaping the coastline. Port construction and operations have altered sediment transport patterns around Gangavaram, while changes in sediment supply near Gosthani river mouth have influenced shoreline movement. Varaha river mouth showed substantial accretion, partly linked to breakwater structures and sediment deposition. Rapid urbanisation has further increased vulnerability. Built-up area in the region expanded from 10.64% in 1990 to 38.75% in 2024, while grassland and water bodies declined sharply. The study warned that the loss of natural buffers such as vegetation and wetlands could heighten exposure to coastal hazards. Researchers also found a rising sea-level trend in Visakhapatnam and classified the city as highly vulnerable to sea-level rise. They recommended beach nourishment, seawalls, revetments, breakwaters, mangrove restoration, stricter controls on coastal development and continuous shoreline monitoring. The study was published in the journal Marine Development. title: Lithuania airport shut, Nato jets scramble as 'drone spotted' along Belarus border
text: Authorities advised residents in the Vilnius region to be prepared to seek shelter if necessary, it said. Vilnius airport in Lithuania was temporarily closed and Nato air-policing fighter jets were scrambled after a possible drone was detected flying from the direction of Belarus, Lithuania's National Crisis Control Centre told news agency Reuters. Authorities advised residents in the Vilnius region to be prepared to seek shelter if necessary, it said. The incident comes as security concerns continue to rise across the Baltic region, where countries bordering or located near Russia and Belarus have reported a growing number of airspace incidents linked to the war in Ukraine. Lithuania is a Nato and European Union (EU) member and has been closely monitoring developments along its borders amid concerns about possible Russian aggression. Russia has rejected allegations that it is planning an attack on Nato, while Western officials have said Moscow does not currently have the capability for a direct assault. The development unflods as neighbouring Latvia prepares for a parliamentary election on Saturday, with security concerns featuring prominently in the campaign. Opinion polls have placed Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List at around 14%, narrowly ahead of the overtly pro-Russian Sovereign Power. However, political fragmentation could make it difficult to form a government after the election. Kulbergs, a 47-year-old businessman and amateur rally driver, took office in May after the previous coalition collapsed over its handling of incidents involving military drones that entered Latvian airspace without being detected. The drones were Ukrainian, although Latvian officials blamed Russia for causing them to stray from their intended flight paths. The incident in Lithuania is likely to add to security concerns across the Baltics, where governments have remained on alert over airspace violations and the wider regional impact of the Russia-Ukraine war. title: âArabian Sea will soon be purged of enemy presenceâ: Mojtaba Khamenei warns US
text: Mojtaba Khamenei Iranâs Supreme Leader Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei on Monday warned that foreign forces would soon be pushed out of the Arabian Sea, while asserting that Iranâs armed forces and people remained prepared to confront the countryâs adversaries. In a written message published by Iranian media, Khamenei said enemy forces had been driven back from waters off southern Iran and warned they would not be able to maintain their presence in the Arabian Sea. "Some see us as the fourth superpower in the world. Today, the enemy's forces do not dare to venture beyond the Arabian Sea. Soon the day will come when the Arabian Sea will be purged of their presence. Our people fill the squares and streets across the country with their responsible presence," he said. Watch Mojtaba Khameneiâs Big Warning To US: âArabian Sea Next After Strait Of Hormuz...' The message was issued on the occasion of Iran's "Sacred Defense Week" and the anniversary of the death of Hezbollah leader Sayyid Hassan Nasrallah. It comes amid heightened tensions between Tehran and Washington over the Strait of Hormuz and Iranâs nuclear programme, after US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal linked to reopening the strategic waterway. Khamenei said different sections of Iranian society, despite their apparent differences, were united in supporting the countryâs position, including its claim over the Strait of Hormuz. "Presently, throughout Islamic Iranâadorned by the presence of diverse ethnicitiesâvarious declarations of readiness, particularly armed readiness, exist to construct an arena that will bring renown to them and disgrace to their enemy," he said. He also claimed that Iranian forces had inflicted losses on their adversaries in the waters around the country. "The two southern seas of Iran were the roaming grounds of enemy forces. Today, however, due to the painful blows they have received from the brave warriors and guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they do not advance past the Arabian Sea. Whenever they have braved this danger, they have brought harm upon themselvesâand soon, the Arabian Sea too will be cleared of them," he said. Khamenei further said that sections of Iranian society were standing together to protect what he described as their "rightful positions". "There were days when the enemy constantly tried to weaken the social backbone of the system, but nowadays, various strata of society, despite their apparent differences, stand firm on maintaining their rightful positions, including the preservation of the blessed Strait of Hormuz," he said. Khameneiâs remarks came after Washington rejected Tehranâs proposal linked to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Last week, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi outlined a seven-day proposal under which Iran would reopen the waterway if certain conditions were met by the US. Iran said the proposal was conveyed through intermediaries and linked the reopening to steps including easing US military pressure. On Sunday, US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said Trump had rejected the proposal because Tehran had sought sanctions relief and access to "billions in frozen assets" before entering negotiations on its nuclear programme. Waltz said Washington would ultimately need to reach "some type of agreement" with Iran, but added that Trump would keep all "options on the table". Araghchi disputed Waltzâs account, saying the US ambassador had not seen the proposal. He also said Iran remained open to diplomacy but was prepared for renewed hostilities. "We are fully prepared for the war to be resumed. We stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war. We donât care about U.S. midterm elections. We care about our national interests. At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose," Araghchi said in an interview with NBC's "Meet the Press". In his message, Khamenei also referred to Iranâs past confrontation with foreign powers, accusing them of attempting to weaken the countryâs social and political foundations. "There were days when the hegemonists, through psychological operations and creating an atmosphere of intimidation, emptied the streets of the capital and launched a coup against this nation's quest for independence, subsequently plundering the wealth of this country for 25 years," he said. He said Iranians had demonstrated their support for the countryâs defence efforts over the past seven months. "Yet, for the past seven months, our compatriots across the nation have adorned the squares and streets with their responsible and enthusiastic presence to warm the hearts of the warriors of Islam and cast terror into the enemy's heart," he said. Khamenei also referred to the participation of women in what he described as acts of courage, while asserting that Iranâs past circumstances would not return. "This comparison between the past days and the present days can be expanded further, but in short, as a servant of the dear people of Iran, I declare that those former daysâwhich our enemy dreams of returning toâare gone and will never recur," he said. Nasrallah was killed in an Israeli airstrike on Hezbollahâs main headquarters in Beirutâs southern suburbs on September 28, 2024.
